promise: A query term matches a host only where the host's name actually holds it: inside one label, typed straight through the separators, or read off the label initials.
why: Subsequence over a whole name is too generous once names carry six labels. On a fleet named role.env.product.region.example.com, 'qa' took its q from the role and its a from a label three along, so three terms that named one host returned every host in the product and typing more never narrowed. The highlight had the same bug and hid it: both characters landed under ranges other terms had already painted, so a term matching invisibly looked exactly like a term matching nothing. Anchoring must also not reject a separator a person typed, because every alias the menu displays carries one. Each suite is checked by name for its own passing line: XCTest prints an Executed line per suite, so grepping for a passing one was satisfied by any single suite while another failed, and a mistyped filter name is simply not run and leaves the rest green.
command: out=$(scripts/test.sh --filter RoamingTokenSearchTests --filter AnchoredTokenTests --filter HighlightAgreesWithScoreTests --filter SeparatorBearingQueryTests 2>&1); for s in RoamingTokenSearchTests AnchoredTokenTests HighlightAgreesWithScoreTests SeparatorBearingQueryTests; do printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Test Suite '$s' passed" || exit 1; done
